root_cause: The offcanvas element has data-bs-scroll="true", which prevents the focus trap from being activated, allowing focus to escape when tabbing from the close button.
repair_strategy: Change data-bs-scroll="true" to data-bs-scroll="false" (or remove the attribute) so that the focus trap is activated when the offcanvas is shown, keeping focus inside the panel.

edits.before: <div class="offcanvas offcanvas-end" data-bs-scroll="true" data-bs-backdrop="true" tabindex="-1" id="help" aria-labelledby="help-title">
edits.after: <div class="offcanvas offcanvas-end" data-bs-scroll="false" data-bs-backdrop="true" tabindex="-1" id="help" aria-labelledby="help-title">

expected_accessibility_effect: Focus will remain trapped inside the offcanvas panel when pressing Tab, preventing escape to the underlying page and allowing keyboard users to navigate the help content.
functional_risks: Setting scroll to false disables scrolling of the page background while the offcanvas is open, which could hinder access to content behind the panel if the offcanvas content overflows.
verification_requirements: After opening the help panel with Enter, the first Tab should move focus to the close button.
A second Tab while the panel is open should keep focus inside the panel (cycle back to the close button or other focusable elements).
Verify that scrolling the page background is restricted when the offcanvas is open (optional).
